title: Merge Intervals
summary: Merge all overlapping intervals (touching ones count as overlapping) and return the merged list sorted by start.
statement:
Each `intervals[i] = [start, end]` is a closed interval. Merge every group of overlapping intervals into one and return the resulting non-overlapping intervals sorted by start.

Intervals that only touch, like `[1,4]` and `[4,5]`, overlap and are merged.
hints: After sorting by start, every interval that overlaps the current group comes right after it.
Keep the last merged interval. If the next interval starts at or before its end, extend the end to the larger of the two ends.
Otherwise close the group and start a new one. Sorting dominates: O(n log n).

title: Insert Interval
summary: Insert newInterval into a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals, merging where needed, and return the result still sorted and non-overlapping.
statement:
`intervals` is sorted by start and its intervals do not overlap. Insert `newInterval`, merging it with any intervals it overlaps (touching counts as overlapping), and return the result, still sorted and non-overlapping.

The list may be empty.
constraints: intervals is sorted by start and non-overlapping
hints: The intervals fall into three runs: those entirely before newInterval, those overlapping it, and those entirely after it.
Copy the "before" run (end < new start) as it is.
Merge every overlapping interval into newInterval by taking the minimum start and maximum end, add the merged interval, then copy the rest. O(n).

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Return the fewest intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap. Intervals that only touch at an end do not overlap.
statement:
Return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove from `intervals` so that the remaining intervals do not overlap.

Intervals that only touch at a point, like `[1,2]` and `[2,3]`, do not overlap.
hints: Flip it: keep as many intervals as possible; the rest must be removed.
Greedy, like activity selection: among intervals that fit, keep the one that ends earliest, because it leaves the most room for the rest.
Sort by end. Keep an interval if its start ≥ the end of the last kept one; otherwise count it as removed.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
summary: Each balloon spans [start, end] on the x-axis. A vertical arrow at x bursts every balloon with start ≤ x ≤ end. Return the fewest arrows to burst them all. Values can be as large as ±2^31.
statement:
Each balloon is a horizontal segment `[start, end]` on the x-axis. An arrow shot straight up at position `x` bursts every balloon with `start ≤ x ≤ end`.

Return the minimum number of arrows needed to burst every balloon.
hints: Shooting at the end of the balloon that ends first bursts as many others as possible.
Sort by end. Shoot at the first end, skip every balloon that starts at or before that position, and shoot again at the next one's end.
Values reach ±2³¹, so compare with Integer.compare in the comparator: a − b overflows.

title: Interval List Intersections
summary: Two lists of closed intervals are each sorted and pairwise disjoint. Return every intersection between them, in order.
statement:
`firstList` and `secondList` are lists of closed intervals. Each list is sorted and its intervals are pairwise disjoint.

Return the intersections of the two lists: every interval where some interval of the first list overlaps some interval of the second, in sorted order. Intersections can be single points such as `[5,5]`.
constraints: Each list is sorted and pairwise disjoint
hints: Walk both lists with two pointers, like merging.
Two intervals overlap on [max(starts), min(ends)] when that start ≤ that end.
Then advance the pointer whose interval ends first: it cannot overlap anything further in the other list.

title: Remove Covered Intervals
summary: Remove every interval [a, b) covered by another [c, d) (c ≤ a and b ≤ d). Return how many remain.
statement:
Interval `[a, b)` is covered by interval `[c, d)` if `c ≤ a` and `b ≤ d`. Remove every interval covered by another interval in the list and return how many remain.

All intervals are distinct.
hints: Sort so that any interval that could cover another comes before it.
Sort by start ascending and, for equal starts, by end descending. Then an interval is covered exactly when its end ≤ the largest end seen so far.
Count the intervals that extend past the running maximum end.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
summary: For each query q, return the size (right − left + 1) of the smallest interval with left ≤ q ≤ right, or -1 if none contains it.
statement:
Each `intervals[i] = [left, right]` has size `right − left + 1`. For each `queries[j]`, return the size of the smallest interval that contains it (`left ≤ q ≤ right`), or `-1` if no interval contains it.

Return the answers in the order of the queries.
hints: Checking every interval for every query is O(n·q). Answer the queries in sorted order instead.
Sort the intervals by left and the queries by value (remembering their original positions). Sweep: push every interval with left ≤ q into a min-heap ordered by size.
Pop intervals from the top of the heap whose right < q; they can never help a later query. The top, if any, is the answer for q.
